You are working in the git repository checked out at /luxon (the Luxon date/time library, JavaScript, jest tests). Do NOT use the internet. Do NOT look at any other copy of luxon (e.g. node_modules copies) for reference beyond what is in /luxon/src and /luxon/test.

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/interval.js so that `Interval.fromISO` works correctly when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true. A hidden test named "Interval.fromISO works with Settings.throwOnInvalid" must pass. The bug: `Interval.fromISO(text, opts)` calls `DateTime.fromISO(s, opts)` / `DateTime.fromISO(e, opts)` and `Duration.fromISO(...)` directly. When `Settings.throwOnInvalid === true`, those calls THROW (InvalidDateTimeError / InvalidDurationError) instead of returning an invalid instance, so `Interval.fromISO("2016-05-25/PT1H")` (start/duration form) or `Interval.fromISO("PT1H/2016-05-25")` (duration/end form) throws even though it should return a valid Interval. Also `Interval.fromISO("garbage")` should throw InvalidIntervalError (that part is expected).

REQUIRED FIX APPROACH (mirror upstream): in `static fromISO(text, opts)`, parse the start and end DateTimes inside try/catch blocks, recording `startIsValid`/`endIsValid` booleans, then use those booleans for the control flow instead of `start.isValid`/`end.isValid`. Keep the existing final `Interval.invalid("unparsable", ...)` return. Make sure the duration branch also behaves sanely when throwOnInvalid is true (e.g. wrap the `Duration.fromISO` calls in try/catch too, or otherwise ensure a non-parsable duration does not throw an unexpected error type; prefer the minimal change that keeps `Interval.fromISO` returning/behaving correctly).

STEPS:
1. First run the baseline test suite and record results: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -60` (also run `npx jest test/interval` ). Record exactly which tests fail BEFORE your change.
2. Apply the fix with edit_file on /luxon/src/interval.js only. Do not touch any test file. Do not reformat unrelated code.
3. Run `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -60` again and confirm: (a) no test that passed before now fails, (b) the interval tests all pass. Also write a scratch check (e.g. a temp file /tmp/check.js run with `npx jest` or `node -r @babel/register`) that verifies with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`: `Interval.fromISO("2016-05-25/PT1H")` returns a valid interval, `Interval.fromISO("PT1H/2016-05-25")` returns a valid interval, `Interval.fromISO("2016-05-25/2016-05-26")` works, and `Interval.fromISO("nonsense")` throws InvalidIntervalError. Delete the temp file afterwards.
4. Also run eslint if configured: `cd /luxon && npx eslint src/interval.js`.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff you applied (git diff), the baseline failing tests, the post-fix test results, and the results of your scratch checks. Do not modify anything outside /luxon/src/interval.js.

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/impl/util.js so that a hidden test named "DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February" passes. Only /luxon/src/impl/util.js may be modified. Do NOT modify or delete any test file, and do not reformat unrelated code.

DIAGNOSIS (already established, verify it yourself): `objToLocalTS(obj)` in /luxon/src/impl/util.js builds `Date.UTC(obj.year, obj.month-1, obj.day, ...)` and, for years 0..99, undoes JS's 19XX interpretation with `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`. That is wrong when `obj.day` overflows the month (e.g. day=92 for December): the day overflow is first resolved in the 19XX/20XX calendar (where February can have 29 days, e.g. year 2000 is a leap year) and only then is the year changed, so the result can be off by a day when the target year's February has a different number of days (e.g. year 100 is not a leap year). Example: DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 61 }) should be 0100-03-02 but currently comes out as 0100-03-01.

REQUIRED FIX: in `objToLocalTS`, inside the `if (obj.year < 100 && obj.year >= 0)` branch, replace the year-only adjustment with one that re-applies the month and day so the overflow is recomputed in the correct calendar, i.e.:

    d = new Date(d);
    // set the month and day again, this is necessary because year 2000 is a leap year, but year 100 is not
    d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day);

(keep `let d = Date.UTC(...)` and `return +d;` as they are).

STEPS:
1. Run the baseline suite first and record failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40`. Note: there are 2 known pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French locale hour padding) that must remain the ONLY failures.
2. Apply the edit to /luxon/src/impl/util.js only.
3. Re-run `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40` and confirm the same 2 pre-existing failures and nothing new. Also run `npx jest test/datetime test/interval test/zones test/info`.
4. Verify behaviour with a scratch script (create /tmp/check100.js, run with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/check100.js` or via a temporary jest test file placed in /tmp and run with `npx jest --rootDir /luxon /tmp/...` if simpler; if you must create a temp test inside the repo, delete it afterwards and make sure `git status --porcelain` shows only ` M src/impl/util.js` at the end):
   - DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 61 }) -> year 100, month 3, day 2
   - DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 2 }) -> year 100, month 1, day 2 (existing test must still pass)
   - DateTime.fromISO("0100-01-02").minus({ days: 2 }) -> year 99, month 12, day 31 (existing test must still pass)
   - DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ months: 2 }) -> year 100, month 2, day 28
   - DateTime.fromISO("0099-01-31").plus({ months: 1 }) -> year 99, month 2, day 28
   - DateTime.fromISO("0099-02-28").plus({ days: 1 }) -> year 99, month 3, day 1
   - DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 60 }) -> year 100, month 3, day 1
   - Also sanity check a normal modern date: DateTime.fromISO("2016-03-12T10:13").plus({ days: 1, hours: 3, minutes: 28 }) still gives 2016-03-13T13:41.
5. Run `npx eslint src/impl/util.js`.

REPORT BACK: the exact `git diff` you applied, baseline vs post-fix jest summary, the scratch-check outputs, and confirmation that `git status --porcelain` shows only ` M src/impl/util.js`.

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js so that two hidden tests pass: "FixedOffsetZone is invalid when constructed with a non-numeric offset" and "A DateTime in an invalid FixedOffsetZone is itself invalid". Only /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js may be modified. Do NOT modify or delete any test file, and do not reformat unrelated code. NOTE: other agents are concurrently editing src/interval.js, src/impl/util.js, src/datetime.js and src/duration.js — leave those alone.

DIAGNOSIS (verify it yourself): the class hardcodes validity:

    /** @override **/
    get isValid() {
      return true;
    }

So `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` claims to be valid, and `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("blorp") })` (or `.setZone(...)`) is wrongly considered valid instead of invalid. Compare with the other zone classes (src/zones/invalidZone.js, src/zones/IANAZone.js) and with src/impl/zoneUtil.js which rely on `zone.isValid`.

REQUIRED FIX: import `isNumber` from "../impl/util.js" (the file already imports `formatOffset, signedOffset` from there — just add isNumber to that import list) and change the isValid getter to:

    /** @override **/
    get isValid() {
      return isNumber(this.fixed);
    }

Do not change anything else in the file (do not touch name, offset, formatOffset, etc.).

STEPS:
1. Run the baseline suite first and record failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40`. Known pre-existing failures: 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French locale hour padding). Those must remain the ONLY failures.
2. Apply the edit to /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js only.
3. Re-run `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40` and confirm no new failures; also run `npx jest test/zones test/info test/datetime`.
4. Verify with a scratch script (create /tmp/checkzone.js, run with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/checkzone.js` importing from a RELATIVE path like "./src/luxon.js" since absolute imports may not resolve; delete it afterwards and make sure `git status --porcelain` shows no new untracked files of yours):
   - `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp").isValid === false`
   - `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("blorp") }).isValid === false`
   - `DateTime.local().setZone(new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")).isValid === false`
   - `FixedOffsetZone.utcInstance.isValid === true`, `FixedOffsetZone.instance(5).isValid === true`, `FixedOffsetZone.parseSpecifier("UTC+6").isValid === true`
   - `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance(300) }).toISO()` still works and equals "1970-01-01T05:00:00.000+05:00"
   - Existing test expectations in test/zones/fixedOffset.test.js and test/info/zones.test.js still pass.
5. Run `npx eslint src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js`.

REPORT BACK: the exact `git diff` for /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js, baseline vs post-fix jest summary, the scratch-check outputs, and confirmation that no test files were touched and you left no untracked files behind.

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/duration.js so that a hidden test named "Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs" passes. Only /luxon/src/duration.js may be modified. Do NOT modify or delete any test file, and do not reformat unrelated code.

DIAGNOSIS (verify it yourself): the conversion matrices at the top of /luxon/src/duration.js must contain an entry for every (larger unit -> smaller unit) pair. In `casualMatrix`, the `quarters` entry is:

    quarters: {
      months: 3,
      weeks: 13,
      days: 91,
      hours: 91 * 24,
      minutes: 91 * 24 * 60,
      milliseconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
    },

It is MISSING `seconds`, while every other entry (years, months, and the accurateMatrix quarters) has all the smaller units including seconds. Because of that, converting quarters to seconds fails: e.g. `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).normalize()` or `.shiftTo("seconds")` produces NaN / wrong results, and `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).as("seconds")` is NaN.

REQUIRED FIX: add the missing `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60,` line to the `quarters` entry of `casualMatrix`, keeping the existing key order (months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds) and matching the style of the `years`/`months` entries. Do not change any other matrix entry.

STEPS:
1. Run the baseline suite first and record failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40`. Known pre-existing failures: 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French locale hour padding). Those must remain the ONLY failures.
2. Apply the edit to /luxon/src/duration.js only.
3. Re-run `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40` and confirm no new failures; also run `npx jest test/duration`.
4. Verify with a scratch script (create /tmp/checkdur.js, run with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/checkdur.js`; delete it afterwards and make sure `git status --porcelain` shows only the expected modified files: src/interval.js, src/impl/util.js, src/datetime.js, src/duration.js — the first three are other agents' concurrent work, leave them alone):
   - For every ordered pair of units [years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds], check that `Duration.fromObject({ [big]: 1 }).as(small)` is a finite positive number and that `Duration.fromObject({ [big]: 1, [small]: 0 }).normalize().as(small)` equals that number (within a small epsilon). Print any pair that yields NaN or a mismatch.
   - Specifically check `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).as("seconds")` === 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 and that `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).shiftTo("seconds").seconds` === 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 + 1.
   - Confirm existing expectations still hold: Duration.fromObject({ years: 2, days: -2 }).normalize().toObject() equals { years: 1, days: 363 }; Duration.fromObject({ years: 2, days: 5000 }).normalize().toObject() equals { years: 15, days: 255 }.
5. Run `npx eslint src/duration.js`.

REPORT BACK: the exact `git diff` you applied, baseline vs post-fix jest summary, the scratch-check outputs (including any mismatching unit pairs), and confirmation that `git status --porcelain` shows only modified src files and no new untracked files.
